```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
set.seed(1)
```


## Q1 Birthday Simulation
```{r}
# Randomly sample n birthdays from 1–365. If the number of unique birthdays is less than n, then True at least two people share the same birthday; if false, unique birthdays number should = n.

birthday_sim = function(n) {

  birthdays = sample(1:365, size = n, replace = TRUE)

  n_unique = length(unique(birthdays))

  same_birthday = n_unique < n

  same_birthday
}
# Test
birthday_sim(2)

birthday_sim(10)

birthday_sim(50)

birthday_sim(365)
```

```{r}
# 10,000 simulations
birthday_df =
  expand_grid(
    group_size = 2:50,
    iter = 1:10000
  )

birthday_df

birthday_results =
  birthday_df |>
  mutate(
    same_birthday = map_lgl(group_size, birthday_sim)
  )

birthday_results

# Probability
birthday_stat =
  birthday_results |>
  group_by(group_size) |>
  summarize(
    probability = mean(same_birthday)
  )

birthday_stat |>
  ggplot(aes(x = group_size, y = probability)) +
  geom_line(color = "seagreen", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Probability of Shared Birthdays by Group Size",
    x = "Group Size",
    y = "Probability of Shared Birthday"
  )
```
The probability of at least two people sharing a birthday increases with group size. This result makes sense because larger groups contain more people, increasing the chance of shared birthdays. The probability approaches 1 but does not reach 1 within the simulated group sizes, since there is still a small chance that everyone has a different birthday.


## Q2 Longitudinal Study
```{r}
# List files
participant =
  tibble(files = list.files("data/data/"))

participant =
  participant |>
  mutate(
    path = str_c("data/data/", files))

participant

# Read files and save as new variable
participant =
  participant |>
  mutate(data = map(path, read_csv)
  )

participant
```

```{r}
# Tidy-up: Unnest → Extract group → Reshape weekly data (wide to long) → Finalize
participant_tidy =
  participant |>
  unnest(data)

participant_tidy =
  participant_tidy |>
  mutate(
    group = str_sub(files, 1, 3),
    subj = str_sub(files, 1, 6))

participant_tidy =
  participant_tidy |>
  mutate(
    group = str_sub(files, 1, 3))

participant_tidy =
  participant_tidy |>
  pivot_longer(
    week_1:week_8,
    names_to = "week",
    values_to = "outcome",
    names_prefix = "week_"
  )

participant_tidy =
  participant_tidy |>
  select(
    group,
    subj = files,
    week,
    outcome)

participant_tidy

# Subject ID revision
participant_tidy =
  participant_tidy |>
  mutate(
    subj = str_replace(subj, ".csv", ""))

participant_tidy
```

```{r}
# Plot
participant_tidy |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome,
             group = subj, color = group)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  facet_grid(~group) +
  labs(
    title = "Longitudinal Outcomes by Study Group",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome")

# No noticeable difference in the plot whether week treated as character or numeric, but technically it should be numerical to represents time
participant_tidy =
  participant_tidy |>
  mutate(
    week = as.numeric(week)
  )

participant_tidy |>
  ggplot(aes(x = week, y = outcome,
             group = subj, color = group)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_path() +
  facet_grid(~group) +
  labs(
    title = "Longitudinal Outcomes by Study Group",
    x = "Week",
    y = "Outcome")
```
The control group shows fluctuations in outcome over time around approximately 1.25, while the experimental group shows a generally increasing trend across the eight weeks with higher outcome values toward the end of the study.
